analyst_view.overall: Werder Bremen (6th, 18 points, unbeaten in five home games) host bottom side Gladbach (4 points from 10, in the relegation zone) on Friday night, five days after a 4-0 Nordderby win over Hamburg; neither side played in midweek and it should be around -1°C at kick-off. Werder are without Marco Grüll, their top assist man (calf), and coach Daniel Thioune is 'very critical' about Justin Njinmah (muscle), who scored twice against Hamburg; the numbers know about neither, while they still take off Mitchell Weiser, who has trained fully and returns to the squad. For Gladbach, Robin Hack is out with a muscle problem (not in the numbers), while captain Tim Kleindienst and Hugo Bolin trained all week and could be involved, Alexander Blessin decides on Friday; the numbers count both as out. Gladbach have become a deep, hard-to-break side under Blessin, and Felix Zwayer, a referee who shows plenty of cards, is in charge (already counted).

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, 1.9 for Werder, and already take off Weiser (now likely to play, a small plus back) and Bolin and Ullrich for Gladbach. What they do not see is that Grüll, Werder's main creator, is out and Njinmah is unlikely to make it, and that Hack, one of Gladbach's few threats, is out; Kleindienst and Bolin may return but only from the bench after injury. Against a Gladbach side that now sits deep, that pulls a little lower, to about 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, 5.4 for Werder, and already count Gladbach's habit of conceding corners lately (37 in six). Weiser's return gives Werder back their right-sided crossing, while Grüll's absence and Agu still being out on the left take some away; Gladbach defending deep tends to give away corners. These balance, so I stay at about 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards, a high figure because they already add about 28% for Felix Zwayer (4.7 cards a game) and 8% for Gladbach's 20 cards in their last six, the sign of a side scrapping at the bottom. Werder's own card count is low and this is no derby, and nothing new on top of what is counted points either way, so I stay at about 5.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.4 shots, 18.3 for Werder, already lifted 11% for Werder's 105 shots in six games. Without Grüll and probably Njinmah, and with Hack out for Gladbach, both attacks lose a regular shooter that the numbers still count on, which Weiser's return only partly makes up, so I trim slightly to about 30.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.2 shots on target, 7.0 for Werder, already boosted for Werder's sharp recent finishing (39 on target in six, Njinmah's two goals against Hamburg among them). With Njinmah unlikely and Grüll out, and Gladbach's attack thin without Hack and with Kleindienst short of fitness, I take a little off, to about 10.9.
